successCriteria.description: GET /employees/me returns HTTP 200 with the authenticated actor's profile in the EmployeeProfile shape (id, employeeNumber, firstName, lastName, email, role, managerId, department, hireDate, employmentStatus), and the response body never contains passwordHash or terminationDate.
employeeRoutes is re-exported from src/modules/employee/index.ts and registered on the Fastify app in src/app.ts so the endpoint is reachable at runtime.
A missing/invalid request.user yields 401 UnauthorizedError, and an unknown employee id yields 404 NotFoundError, both mapped to { error, code } via the AppError contract.

constraints: No controller file — the route calls employeeService.getEmployeeProfileById directly, matching the existing leave/balance/auth route shape.
The route is read-only: it must not open a transaction, write an audit record, or mutate any state.
resolveActor and sendError are local copies in employee.routes.ts (not imported from leave.routes.ts), matching the balance/auth precedent.
The service instance is resolved from fastify.employeeService if present, else new EmployeeService(new PgEmployeeRepository()) — there is no createEmployeeService factory.
The actor id is taken from request.user (verified token), never from a client-supplied body/query/param.
outOfScope: scripts/smoke.js extension (login + authenticated read probes) — owned by Sub-phase 7.2.
Any change to EmployeeService.getEmployeeProfileById / toEmployeeProfile mapping, EmployeeProfile type, or the employee repository — delivered in Phase 2 and treated as fixed contracts.

entityInvariants.invariant: The profile returned by GET /employees/me is the EmployeeProfile shape from src/shared/types and must never expose passwordHash or terminationDate, regardless of the underlying Employee row.
The authenticated actor's identity (id) is derived solely from the verified token's request.user; the route never accepts or trusts a client-supplied employee id.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Caller must be authenticated (valid request.user with id + EmployeeRole); the id passed is the actor's own id from the token.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Unknown id -> NotFoundError (404); missing/invalid actor -> UnauthorizedError (401); both mapped to { error, code }.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The resolveActor/sendError helper shape (AppError -> { error, code } with correct status, else 500) must match the existing implementation in leave.routes.ts, using local copies rather than imports.
The returned profile must be the EmployeeProfile type (no passwordHash/terminationDate) as produced by EmployeeService.getEmployeeProfileById via toEmployeeProfile.
request.user shape { id: string; role: EmployeeRole } and EmployeeRole enum membership must match the auth contract populated by registerAuth.
AppError subclasses (UnauthorizedError, NotFoundError) and their code strings must be the shared error contract, not re-declared locally.

integrationPoints.why: The route delegates profile resolution to the service, which owns the toEmployeeProfile mapping that strips passwordHash/terminationDate.
Populates request.user { id, role } from the verified JWT; the route's resolveActor consumes this contract.
employeeRoutes must be registered after registerAuth so the auth preHandler applies and the endpoint is reachable.
